questions.question: A shock wave angled 90? from the relative flow is a:
questions.explanation: A wave perpendicular to the upstream relative flow is a normal shock; an oblique shock is inclined at another angle.

questions.question: Find the Reynolds number for an airplane wing with a 4 ft chord moving at 120 mi/h under standard atmospheric conditions.
questions.explanation: Use Re = ?Vc/?. At standard sea-level conditions, V = 176 ft/s and c = 4 ft give Re ? 4.48 ? 10?, matching option A.

questions.question: An airplane is making a 40? banked turn of 565 ft radius. What should its airspeed be?
questions.explanation: For a coordinated level turn, tan ? = V?/(gR). Thus V = ?(gR tan 40?) ? 123.6 ft/s, matching 123.50 ft/s.

questions.question: The aspect ratio of a wing is calculated by:
choices: Wing area divided by wing span
Wing span divided by wing thickness
Wing area divided by wing chord
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio is span squared divided by planform area; for a rectangular wing this reduces to span divided by chord.

questions.question: In a 45? bank, what is the load factor experienced by the aircraft?
questions.explanation: In a level coordinated turn, n = 1/cos ?. At 45?, n ? 1.414, or 1.4.

questions.question: What is the total force of a 40 mi/h wind on a hangar door 40 ft by 20 ft?
questions.explanation: At standard sea-level density, q = ??V? = ?(0.002377)(40 ? 5280/3600)? ? 4.09 lb/ft?. The 40 ? 20 ft door has area 800 ft?, so F = qA ? 3,272 lb. This assumes a drag coefficient of 1.0; the original choices did not include this result.

questions.question: An airplane is at a pressure altitude of 33,500 ft and a density altitude of 32,000 ft. Calculate the outside air temperature.
questions.explanation: At 33,500 ft, ISA pressure is about 25.6 kPa. The density at a 32,000 ft density altitude is about 0.425 kg/m?; at the given pressure this implies T ? 209.6 K = 377.2 ?R. The nearest option is 378 ?R. A density altitude below pressure altitude indicates colder-than-ISA air.

questions.question: Lift on the wing is most properly defined as:
choices: Force perpendicular to the relative wind
Reduced pressure resulting from laminar flow over the upper camber of an airfoil
Force parallel to the relative wind
Pressure differential acting perpendicular to the wing
questions.answerText: Force perpendicular to the relative wind
questions.explanation: Lift is the aerodynamic force component perpendicular to the relative wind. It is not defined by a particular flow regime or surface pressure alone.

questions.question: For isentropic flow over an airfoil, the freestream temperature and pressure are 245 K and 114.66, respectively. At a point on the airfoil, pressure is 3.6 ? 10? Pa. Calculate the density at that point.
questions.explanation: Convert 114.66 psi to about 790.6 kPa. For isentropic air, T?/T? = (p?/p?)^((??1)/?), so T? ? 101.4 K. Then ?? = p?/(RT?) = 36,000/(287 ? 101.4) ? 1.24 kg/m?, matching 1.23 kg/m? (B).

questions.question: What is the maximum obtainable efficiency of a propeller if the airspeed is 210 knots and slipstream velocity is 230 knots?
questions.explanation: The ideal propeller efficiency is 2V/(V + V_s). Substituting 210 and 230 kt gives 420/440 ? 95.5%, or 95%.

questions.question: A standard altimeter reads 14,000 ft. When the ambient temperature is 35?F, what is the density altitude?
questions.explanation: The temperature is warmer than ISA at 14,000 ft, so density altitude is higher than pressure altitude. The standard correction gives approximately 15,656 ft.

questions.question: For an airplane flying at 886 ft/s at 25,000 ft altitude, find the critical value of the pressure coefficient.
questions.explanation: At 25,000 ft, ISA temperature is about 238.6 K and speed of sound about 1,016 ft/s, so M? ? 0.872. The isentropic pressure ratio for a sonic point gives p*/p? ? 0.867. Thus Cp,crit = 2(p*/p? ? 1)/(?M??) ? ?0.250, matching ?0.25 (A).

questions.question: A Clark Y wing 350 ft? in area is moving through the air at 80 ft/s. Determine the drag (CD = 0.0452).
questions.explanation: D = qSCD, with q = ??V? and sea-level density ? ? 0.002377 slug/ft?. This gives D ? 120 lb.

questions.question: As the cyclic control is moved forward, the rotor disc tilts forward. The helicopter will:
questions.explanation: Tilting the rotor disc forward produces a forward horizontal thrust component, so the helicopter moves forward.

questions.question: Which speed gives the best rate of climb and is used to gain the most altitude in a given period of time?
questions.explanation: VY is the best-rate-of-climb speed: it gives the greatest altitude gain per unit time. VX instead gives the greatest altitude gain per unit horizontal distance.

questions.question: Rotor blade loading is the rotor thrust divided by the total planform area of the rotor blades. Which term describes this quantity?
questions.explanation: Blade loading is rotor thrust divided by the combined blade planform area. Disc loading instead divides rotor thrust by the rotor swept-disc area.

questions.question: An airplane weighing 3,000 lb has a wing area of 350 ft?. What horsepower is required for the wing when flying at 90 ft/s? (CD = 0.0561)
questions.explanation: At sea level, q = ??V? = ?(0.002377)(90)? ? 9.63 lb/ft?. Then D = qSCD = 9.63(350)(0.0561) ? 189 lb, and required power is DV/550 ? 30.9 hp, which rounds to 31 hp.

questions.question: Across a normal shock, what happens to the static pressure and temperature?
questions.explanation: A normal shock compresses and heats the flow: static pressure and static temperature both increase, while velocity and Mach number decrease.

questions.question: The angle of attack of an airfoil is the angle between the:
choices: Longitudinal axis and the relative wind
Airfoil's center line and the relative wind
Airfoil's center line and the longitudinal axis
Chord line of the wing and the relative wind
questions.answerText: Chord line of the wing and the relative wind
questions.explanation: Angle of attack is measured between the airfoil chord line and the relative wind. The source text for this item is encoded oddly in the PDF; wording has been normalized.

questions.question: For a conventional cambered airfoil below stall, as angle of attack increases, the center of pressure generally moves:
questions.explanation: For a conventional cambered airfoil in its normal pre-stall range, increasing angle of attack generally shifts the center of pressure forward. The exact movement depends on airfoil shape and operating range.

questions.question: If the aircraft is operated in steady flight at maximum lift-to-drag ratio, the total drag is:
questions.explanation: Maximum L/D is the condition of minimum drag for a given lift in steady flight.

questions.question: What is the primary factor in determining calibrated airspeed?
questions.explanation: Calibrated airspeed is indicated airspeed corrected for instrument and position errors. Wind does not affect airspeed, and density is used in converting to true airspeed.

questions.question: What is the definition of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, or work transferred per unit time.

questions.question: Roll is defined as movement of the lateral axis about which axis?
questions.explanation: Roll is rotation about the aircraft's longitudinal axis.

questions.question: Pitch is defined as movement of the longitudinal axis about which axis?
questions.explanation: Pitch is rotation about the lateral axis.

questions.question: Yaw is defined as movement of the directional axis about which axis?
questions.explanation: Yaw is rotation about the vertical axis.

questions.question: All motion or changes in aircraft attitude occur about which position?
questions.explanation: Aircraft rotations are described about the center of gravity, where the three body axes are taken to intersect.

questions.question: A horizontal pipe, 1 ft in diameter, tapers gradually to 8 in. in diameter. If the flow rate is 9 ft?/s, what is the pressure difference between the two sections?
questions.explanation: Continuity gives V? = Q/A? = 9/(?/4) ? 11.46 ft/s and V? = 9/[?(8/12)?/4] ? 25.78 ft/s. For a horizontal pipe, ?p = ??(V?? ? V??); using water density gives ?p ? 3.59 psi. The PDF wording is split across lines, but the stated 9 ft?/s flow rate reproduces option B.

questions.question: Which flight condition has both supersonic and subsonic airflow around the aircraft?
questions.explanation: Transonic flow occurs near Mach 1, where local regions may be both subsonic and supersonic. Mach 1.1 is the closest listed condition.

questions.question: What is the line from the leading edge to the trailing edge of an airfoil that is equidistant from its upper and lower surfaces?
questions.explanation: The mean camber line is the locus of points halfway between the upper and lower surfaces, measured perpendicular to the chord.

questions.question: An airplane is flying at sea level at 160 knots. What is the difference between stagnation and static pressure in the pitot-static system?
questions.explanation: At low Mach number, the pressure difference is dynamic pressure q = ??V?. With 160 kt converted to SI units and sea-level density, q ? 4,150 Pa.

questions.question: At an altitude in ISA, the speed of sound is 678 mi/h. What is the altitude?
questions.explanation: Convert 678 mi/h to about 303 m/s. From a = ?(?RT), this corresponds to T ? 228.4 K. Using the ISA tropospheric lapse rate, h = (288.15 ? 228.4)/0.0065 ? 9.2 km; the nearest listed value is 9,180 m.

questions.question: A convergent duct has an inlet area of 5 m?. Air enters at 10 m/s and leaves at 98.43 ft/s. What is the exit area?
questions.explanation: For incompressible flow, A?V? = A?V?. Convert 98.43 ft/s to 30 m/s; A? = 5(10/30) ? 1.667 m?.

questions.question: An airplane flies at 130 mi/h at a standard altitude of 5,000 ft. At a point on the wing, pressure is 1,750 lb/ft?. Calculate velocity at that point, assuming incompressible flow.
questions.explanation: At 5,000 ft, ISA static pressure is about 1,760.8 lb/ft? and density is about 0.002048 slug/ft?. The freestream speed is 130 mi/h = 190.7 ft/s. Bernoulli gives V? = ?[V?? + 2(p? ? p?)/?] ? 216.6 ft/s for p? = 1,750 lb/ft?, matching 216.8 ft/s (D).

questions.question: A Pitot tube is mounted in the test section of a low-speed subsonic wind tunnel. The flow velocity, static pressure, and temperature are 150 mi/h, 1 atm, and 70?F. Calculate the pressure measured by the Pitot tube.
questions.explanation: The Pitot reading is stagnation pressure: p? = p + ??V?. The dynamic pressure at 150 mi/h is about 56 psf, so p? ? 2,172 psf.

questions.question: A cylinder 3 ft in diameter and 8 ft long rotates at 150 rpm in an air stream of 50 mi/h. What is the total lift?
questions.explanation: Using the Magnus-effect circulation ? = 2?r?? and lift per unit length L? = ?V? gives a total lift close to 310 lb for the stated span.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an equation for calculating aspect ratio?
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio is b?/S, equivalent to b/c for a rectangular wing and S/c? for S = bc. The expression b?/c? is the square of b/c, not the aspect ratio.

questions.question: In a Venturi tube, point A has diameter 1 ft and point B has radius 3 in. What is the flow rate of water if the pressure difference is 5 in. of mercury?
questions.explanation: A 5 in. Hg pressure difference is about 5.67 ft of water head. With A? = ?(1 ft)?/4 and A? = ?(0.5 ft)?/4, Bernoulli plus continuity gives Q ? 3.87 ft?/s (about 0.110 m?/s). The PDF labels its answer choices m?/s, but those units are inconsistent with the values.

questions.question: The force against an automobile windshield is 0.012 lb when the car is moving at 1 mi/h. What is the force when it travels at 35 mi/h?
questions.explanation: Aerodynamic force varies with speed squared. F? = 0.012(35/1)? = 14.7 lb.

questions.question: A cylinder 4 ft in diameter and 1 ft long rotates at 100 rpm in an air stream of 40 mi/h. What is the lifting force?
questions.explanation: Using Magnus lift per span, L? = ?V? with ? = 2?r??, gives approximately 36.7 lb for the one-foot cylinder length.

questions.question: This situation happens every time the helicopter's main rotor is at rest.
questions.explanation: With no rotation to provide centrifugal stiffening, rotor blades droop under their own weight.

questions.question: For unaccelerated flight at the same weight, which comparison is true?
choices: Lift is always greater than weight
Lift is always perpendicular to the airfoil chord
Lift is greater during level flight than level turning flight
Lift is greater during level flight than climbing flight
questions.answerText: Lift is greater during level flight than climbing flight
questions.explanation: In steady level flight, lift equals weight. In a steady climb at flight-path angle ?, lift is approximately W cos ? (assuming thrust acts along the flight path), which is less than W. Thus lift in level flight is greater than in the climb.

questions.question: Which vehicle carries its oxidizer instead of taking oxygen from the surrounding air?
questions.explanation: A rocket carries both fuel and oxidizer, so it can produce thrust without atmospheric oxygen. Conventional airplane and helicopter engines use air from the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which assumption applies to the classical incompressible form of Bernoulli?s equation?
choices: It applies only to turbulent flow
It assumes steady, inviscid, incompressible flow along a streamline
It requires mass not to be conserved
It applies only across shock waves
questions.answerText: It assumes steady, inviscid, incompressible flow along a streamline
questions.explanation: The elementary Bernoulli equation is applied to steady, inviscid, incompressible flow along a streamline. More general energy equations can handle compressible flow, so this assumption is specific to the classical incompressible form.

questions.question: It is the design maneuvering speed.
questions.explanation: V_A denotes design maneuvering speed.

questions.question: The aircraft is said to be trimmed if:
choices: The moment at the aerodynamic center is always zero
The rotation at the center of pressure is zero
The net pitching moment about the center of gravity is zero
The net moment about the geometric center is zero
questions.answerText: The net pitching moment about the center of gravity is zero
questions.explanation: In pitch trim, the net pitching moment about the aircraft center of gravity is zero. This is a moment-balance condition; it does not mean angular velocity must be zero in every possible trimmed maneuver.

questions.question: What happens to the value of lift as velocity is doubled?
questions.explanation: With density, wing area, and lift coefficient unchanged, L = ??V?SCL. Doubling V therefore quadruples lift.

questions.question: The rate of climb is RC = 850 ? h/12 ft/min. Compute the climbing time from 300 ft to the service ceiling.
questions.explanation: Using the service-ceiling convention of 100 ft/min gives h = 9,000 ft. Integrating dt = dh/(850 ? h/12) from 300 to 9,000 ft gives about 25.3 min.

questions.question: Airflow passing through an expansion wave:
choices: Increases the pressure of the air
Decreases the temperature of the air
questions.answerText: Decreases the temperature of the air
questions.explanation: An expansion wave accelerates supersonic flow and lowers its static pressure and temperature; density also decreases.

questions.question: An airplane takes 7 min 30 sec to reach 8,000 ft altitude. In the same time interval, it reaches 13,600 ft altitude. Determine the altitude at which power required equals power available.
choices: Cannot be determined from the information provided
questions.answerText: Cannot be determined from the information provided
questions.explanation: The two climb-time statements do not specify the aircraft?s weight, speed, engine/propeller performance, or a climb-performance model. Those data are needed to find where power available equals power required, so none of the four numerical altitudes can be justified from the information given.
